extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, and practitioners (United Kingdom, under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act 1883)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formal rules for preparing, filing, and prosecuting patent applications (provisional and complete), drawings, fees, appeals, and associated forms under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act, 1883 in the United Kingdom. Covers required forms, paper/drawing format, signature/declaration rules, time limits, and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person, whether a British subject or not, may make an application for a patent; two or more persons may make a joint application and a patent may be granted jointly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of filing an application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be left at the Patent Office or sent prepaid by post and must be addressed to the Comptroller, Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where stamped forms are obtainable
rubrics_metrics.description: Stamped forms under the Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Act, 1883, may be obtained at the Inland Revenue Office (Royal Courts of Justice) and at a long list of specified Post Offices throughout the United Kingdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A published list of Post Offices is provided; applicants should use those places to obtain stamped forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration stamp requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'declaration' required on application when made before a justice of the peace does not require an additional stamp; but when made before a Commissioner a 2s. 6d. impressed stamp is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the 2s.6d. stamp is required the application form must be left with the Postmaster at one of the listed Post Offices, who will get the form stamped. In London such forms can also be left at the Inland Revenue Office at the Royal Courts of Justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of application for provisional protection
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for provisional protection consists of: (a) the form of application (Patent Form A or Al, fee 1s. each form), and (b) the form of Provisional specification (Patent Form B) (gratis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of application for complete protection
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for complete protection consists of: (a) the form of application (Patent Form A or Al, fee 1s. each form) and (b) the form of complete specification (Patent Form C) (£3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: There are two application forms: Patent Form A when the application is made by the applicant(s), and Patent Form Al when the invention is a 'communication' from abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to read forms' directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should carefully read the directions upon the forms of application before filling them up to avoid unnecessary trouble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for provisional protection
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for provisional protection continues in force nine months from the date of the application; if a patent is required the complete specification must be left at the Patent Office within nine months from the date of the application for provisional protection or the application will be deemed abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N.B. — A second application form is not required when filing the complete specification following provisional protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must sign the declaration and agent communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'declaration' in the form of application must be signed by the applicant or applicants; all other communications may be made by or through agents duly authorised to the satisfaction of the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper format for specifications and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications and all other documents must be written or printed in large and legible characters upon strong wide-ruled foolscap paper of size 13 inches by 8 inches (on one side only), leaving a margin of two inches on the left-hand part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatures of applicants or agents must be written in a large and legible hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — paper size, borders and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings accompanying provisional or complete specifications must be made upon half-sheets or sheets of imperial drawing paper, to be within a border line of 19 inches by 12 inches or 27 inches by 19 inches, with a margin of 1/2 an inch all round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the drawings will be required upon rolled imperial drawing paper or thin Bristol board of same dimensions as the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — ink, lines, shading, lettering and colour
rubrics_metrics.description: All the lines must be absolutely black, Indian ink of the best quality to be used, and the same strength or colour of the ink maintained throughout the drawing. Any shading must be in lines clearly and distinctly drawn and as open as consistent with effect. Section lines should not be too closely drawn. No colour must be used for any purpose upon the copy of the drawings. All letters and figures of reference must be bold and distinct. The border line should be one fine line only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules are required because drawings are copied by lithography at the Patent Office; strict observance ensures correct copies are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — delivery condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings must not be folded, but must be delivered at the Patent Office either in a perfectly flat state or rolled upon a roller so as to be free from creases or breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings for journal publication
rubrics_metrics.description: After his application has been accepted, every applicant must also furnish the Patent Office with the drawing and concise explanatory statement required by Rule 31 for the preparation of an illustrated journal of patented inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to obtain copies of the Patent Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the Patent Rules (price prepaid, 7s., including postage within the United Kingdom) can be obtained from the Patent Office Sale Branch, 38 Cursitor Street, Chancery Lane, E.C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for copies should be addressed to the Comptroller at that address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term and renewal payment structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent will be granted for the term of 14 years from its date, subject to the payment of £50 before the end of the 4th year and £100 before the end of the 8th year, or in lieu thereof to the payment of annual or renewal fees (specified amounts) commencing before the expiration of the 4th year and extending to and inclusive of the 13th year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exact amounts and options are set out in the Schedule of Fees annexed to the Rules; payments must be made by way of stamped forms obtainable at the listed places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees schedule and specific fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A First Schedule lists fees payable in connection with letters patent: examples include on application for provisional protection (10s.), on filing complete specification (£3), on appeal from Comptroller to Law Officer (by appellant £3), on notice of opposition (by opponent 10s.), on hearings (10s. each party), fees on amendments, renewals, enlargement of time, entries of assignments, duplicates, searches, office copies, certificates, alteration of address, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the full Schedule of Fees for the exact amounts and timing; many fees differ depending on stage (up to sealing or after sealing) and type of proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional/procedural rules for pre-1 Jan 1884 applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications made prior to 1 January 1884 special provisions apply: e.g., the seventh year's payment under prior Letters Patent payable before end of seventh year must be paid as heretofore in one sum of £100; payments previously due in the third year are made payable before the end of the fourth year by the Act of 1883; stamp duties required under the Patent Law Amendment Acts 1852-3 must be paid upon subsequent proceedings in connexion with applications made prior to 1 Jan 1884 up to filing the 'final' specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications under the Acts of 1852-3 must be completed according to their provisions up to the stage of filing the final specification. Patents granted on applications prior to 1 Jan 1884 are exempt from certain provisions of the 1883 Act (e.g., compulsory licences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Law Officer — notice filing time
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person intending to appeal to the law officer from a decision of the Comptroller must, within 14 days from the date of the decision appealed against, file in the Patent Office a notice of such intention (fee payable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appeal shall be entertained if notice is not given within 14 days unless further time is allowed by the Comptroller or by special leave of the law officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal notice contents and service
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall state the nature of the decision appealed against and whether the appeal is from whole or part only (specifying what part). A copy of the notice must be sent to the law officers' clerk and, where there has been opposition before the Comptroller, to the opponent(s), and when the Comptroller refused to seal a patent on ground of pending previous application, to the prior applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form of Notice is provided in Patent Forms; a fee (e.g., £3) is payable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller to transmit papers on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon notice of appeal being filed the Comptroller shall forthwith transmit to the law officers' clerk all papers relating to the matter of the application in respect of which such appeal is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing notice periods and who is notified
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven days' notice, at least, of the time and place appointed for the hearing of any appeal shall be given by the law officers' clerk unless special leave shortens this. Such notice shall be given to the Comptroller and the appellant and, where relevant, to opponent(s) or prior applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence on appeal — scope and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence used on appeal to the law officer shall be the same as that used at the hearing before the Comptroller; no further evidence shall be given, save as to matters which have occurred or come to the knowledge of either party after the date of the decision appealed against, except with leave of the law officer upon application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All documentary evidence required or allowed to be filed by the law officer shall be subject to the same regulations as apply to the procedure before the Comptroller and shall be filed in the Patent Office unless otherwise ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination and conduct money on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The law officer shall, at the request of either party, order the attendance at the hearing on appeal for the purpose of being cross-examined of any person who has made a declaration in the matter unless there is good ground not to order such attendance. Any person requiring attendance of a witness for cross-examination shall tender to the witness a reasonable sum for conduct money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs on appeal and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the law officer orders that costs shall be paid by any party to another he may fix the amount of such costs or direct by whom and in what manner the amount shall be ascertained. If ordered costs are not paid within 14 days after amount fixed or as directed, the party to whom costs are to be paid may apply to the law officer for an order for payment under the provisions of section 38 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such orders may be made a Rule of Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form list and required content of main forms
rubrics_metrics.description: A Second Schedule lists forms (A, Al, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, R, S, T) and their purposes: e.g., Form A Application for Patent; Form Al Application communicated from abroad; Form B Provisional Specification; Form C Complete Specification; Form D Opposition to grant; Form E Application for hearing by Comptroller; Form F Application to amend specification or drawings; Form G Opposition to amendment; Form H Application for compulsory grant of license; Form J Application for Certificate of Payment or Renewal; Form K Application for enlargement of time; Form O Notice of intended exhibition of unpatented invention; Form T Appeal to law officer, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form has prescribed content and notes (e.g., petitions must be examined copies where required) and must be used as specified in the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification — content and claims requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete specification must contain a full description of the invention and in what manner the same is to be performed, and must end with a distinct statement of claims in the form: 'Having now particularly described and ascertained the nature of my said invention, and in what manner the same is to be performed, I declare that what I claim is, ...' followed by distinct statement of the features of novelty claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complete Specification and its duplicate must be signed by the applicant or his agent on the last sheet with the date inserted ('Dated this day of 18__').

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional specification — commencement and formality
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisional specification (Form B) must form the commencement of the Provisional Specification; no stamp is required on this document. Continuation is on wide-ruled foolscap paper (one side only) with a margin of two inches on the left. Provisional Specification and its duplicate must be signed on the last sheet with date inserted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration execution overseas
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the declaration is made out of the United Kingdom the words 'and by virtue of the Statutory Declarations Act, 1835' must be omitted, and the declaration must be made before a British Consular Officer, or where not reasonably practicable, before a public officer duly authorised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and amendment procedures — forms & content
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition to grant (Form D) must state the grounds permitted by section 11 of the Act and be accompanied by an unstamped copy. Applications to amend the specification or drawings (Form F) must state the reasons for amendment and, where the applicant is not the patentee, state the interest he possesses. Opposition to amendment (Form G) must state reason of opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees apply for notices of opposition and hearings (see Schedule of Fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for compulsory grant of licences must clearly set forth the facts of the case and show that the petitioner's interest arises by reason of the default of the patentee to grant licences on reasonable terms; the statement of the case should show as far as possible that the terms of the proposed order are just and reasonable. Paragraphs should be numbered consecutively and the petition should specify the relief claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be accompanied by an examined copy where required and the petition should state grounds under section 22 of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications for certificates, duplicates, entries and alterations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific forms exist for administrative acts: Form J Application for Certificate of Payment or Renewal; Form N Application for Duplicate of Letters Patent (when original destroyed or lost); Form L Request to enter name upon the Register of Patents; Form M Request to enter notification of license in the Register; Form R Notice for alteration of an address in Register; each form prescribes required particulars and accompanying documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various prescribed fees and documentary requirements apply (see Rules and Schedule of Fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending notices/documents to law officers' clerk
rubrics_metrics.description: Any notice or other document required to be given to the law officers' clerk under these rules may be sent by a prepaid letter through the post.
